newsitem.title: USA: US VIEW-U.S. dealers says Australian dollar will recover.
newsitem.headline: US VIEW-U.S. dealers says Australian dollar will recover.

text.p: U.S. financial houses expect the Australian dollar to resume its upward surge after a bout of profit-taking whipped U.S. 2.5 cents from its value this week.
Analysts here were convinced the dollar would return to the top end of 82 cents before the Reserve Bank decides to cut rates again.
They suggested Japanese interest in the dollar was still strong and would help strengthen its value after Tuesday's slump from the mid-81 U.S cent level to 78.55.
"Seems to me the Australian dollar was piggybacking the American dollar," said Anita Lauria from Salomon Bros.
"Same as the U.K. and the Canadian, although Canada flipped way earlier, then you saw the Australia and the sterling both fall victim to profit taking over the last couple of days."
Lauria said that the Australian currency was still "undervalued" and was likely to head back towards 82 cents.
Goldman Sachs analyst John Simpson said the "government seems happy with it in that 78 to 82 cent range".
"What is clear is the importance of Japanese capital inflow," he said.

Global analyst David Hale from Zurich Kemper Investment Inc., who forecast a possible 85 cent dollar earlier this year, said the current state of the commodity market probably meant 82 cents was a little high but "it simply depends on whether the Japanese are there".
Simpson said he expects a Reserve Bank interest rate cut in the first quarter of next year.

One dealer who asked not be named said the market was buzzing with rumours that currency player George Soros had led the push on the Australian dollar but "he wasn't alone by any stretch of the imagination".
